o: Given a JSON object or array whose values are all strings, produce the inverted mapping: original values become keys, original keys (array indices count as keys) become values. Duplicate original values must map to an array of all their keys; unique ones map to the bare key. E.g., {a:"1",b:"2",c:"2",d:"4"} → {1:"a", 2:["b","c"], 4:"d"}; arrays invert through their indices. A single pass with a result map and an Array.isArray check suffices.
k: Iterate Object.keys(obj) so array indices become string keys automatically.
On collision, promote the stored string to an array and push; otherwise store the string.
All values are strings, so no nested recursion is needed.

a.i: Walk every key of obj, read its string value v, and insert into the result: if v absent store the key; if present and already an array push; if present as a string replace with a two-element array.
s: For each key k with value v: handle absent / string / array cases.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the keys with O(1) map operations.

w: On LeetCode this is JavaScript-only; the JS version above is the exact submission format. Pitfalls: forgetting hasOwnProperty (prototype pollution from keys like "constructor"), and remembering arrays iterate with string indices. Follow-up: support nested objects/arrays recursively, or preserve insertion order deterministically.
